notes: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. PATIENT 1, a girl aged 3 at study initiation with KCNT1 p.R474H epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures. Escalating intrathecal doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 6, then maintenance 40 mg every 8 weeks from week 10, INCREASED TO 60 mg every 8 weeks from week 26. Eight weeks after her 9th intrathecal dose she developed vomiting and apparent discomfort; brain and spine imaging two days later revealed SEVERE COMMUNICATING HYDROCEPHALUS with T2 white-matter change representing transependymal flow but no other parenchymal change. She was at her baseline alertness with normal pupils, normal extraocular movements, no sunset eye sign and normal vital signs. Endoscopic third ventriculostomy with choroid plexus cauterisation showed a CSF OPENING PRESSURE OF 55 cm H2O and produced no improvement over the following two days. After considering a ventriculoperitoneal shunt, the family withdrew from the investigational protocol in favour of palliative care; she died under hospice care three months after the final ASO dose. GRADE 3: hydrocephalus requiring intervention, with a fatal outcome. NOTE: hydrocephalus is primarily another lane's scope; included here because the n-of-1 brief explicitly directs extraction of per-patient hydrocephalus events from this literature.

notes: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. PATIENT 2, also a girl aged 3 with KCNT1 p.R474H, enrolled 9 months after patient 1 and about 2 months before hydrocephalus was detected in patient 1. Escalating intrathecal doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg. Brain MRI on day 55 was UNREMARKABLE with normal ventricular size and a normal lumbar opening pressure of 16 cm H2O; repeat MRIs on days 62 and 64 showed MILD INCREASES IN VENTRICULAR SIZE with no evidence of obstruction.
